overview.title: 📖 Overview: Interruptions, Wrong Blessings, and Blessings in Any Language
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 40a–40b
overview.hebrewSource: כׇּל בְּרָכָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ הַזְכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם — אֵינָהּ בְּרָכָה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf begins with talk between hamotzi and the first bite: Rav, Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rav Sheshet draw the line in different places, with Rav Sheshet allowing even 'mix the food for the oxen' because one must feed animals before eating. A run of health advice from Rabbi Ḥiyya and others follows. A new mishna then rules that 'fruit of the ground' works after the fact for tree fruit, 'fruit of the tree' does not work for ground produce, and shehakol works for everything. Rav Huna and Rabbi Yoḥanan argue whether 'everything' includes bread and wine, and Binyamin the shepherd's homemade Aramaic blessing tests what a blessing must contain. The daf ends with a second mishna on foods that do not grow from the ground, and a debate over what novelot are.

slides.title: 🧂 What May Be Said After Hamotzi and Before Eating?
slides.subtitle: Three amora'im, three thresholds for an interruption
rows: No new blessing needed — this serves the blessing
No new blessing — it serves the meal
גַּבֵּיל לְתוֹרֵי — 'Mix the food for the oxen'
No new blessing — one may not eat before feeding his animals, so this too serves the meal

callout.label: Rav Sheshet's source:
callout.text: Rav Yehuda said in Rav's name: it is forbidden to eat before giving food to one's animals, as the verse says first 'I will give grass in your fields for your animals' and only then 'and you shall eat and be satisfied' (Deuteronomy 11:15). Rava bar Shmuel added in Rabbi Ḥiyya's name that one may not break bread until salt or relish is before everyone — yet at the Exilarch's house he broke bread at once, explaining that such refined bread needs no salt.

slides.title: 💊 The Daf's Medicine Cabinet
slides.subtitle: Habits the Sages recommend, and the cautions that go with them

boxes.title: Recommended
items: Rabbi Ḥiyya: after all eating, eat salt; after all drinking, drink water — and you will not be harmed
Baraita: one who inundates his food with water avoids intestinal illness — Rav Ḥisda: a jug per loaf
Rabbi Yoḥanan: lentils once in thirty days keep diphtheria from the house; mustard once in thirty days keeps illness away
Rav: small fish prevent intestinal illness and make the whole body flourish
Rabbi Ḥama son of Rabbi Ḥanina: black cumin prevents heart pain

boxes.title: Cautions
items: Skip the salt or the water: by day, worry about bad breath; by night, about diphtheria
Lentils every day — bad breath; mustard every day — weakness of the heart
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: black cumin is one of sixty deadly drugs; sleep east of its storehouse and your blood is on your own head
Resolution: its taste heals, its odor harms — Rabbi Yirmeya's mother stuck it to his bread for the taste, then peeled it off

callout.label: Also from Rabbi Ḥiyya:
callout.text: Urine leaves the body completely only when seated; Rav Kahana adds that over loose soil, or standing on a high place and aiming downhill, one may stand.

slides.title: 🌳 Said the Wrong Blessing? The Mishna's After-the-Fact Rules
slides.subtitle: A more general blessing can cover a more specific food, but not the reverse

nodes.content: ❓ 'Who creates fruit of the ground' over fruit of the tree — valid?
✅ Valid. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak: the mishna follows Rabbi Yehuda, who holds the land is primary — if the spring dried up and the tree was cut, he still brings first fruits and reads the declaration
❓ 'Who creates fruit of the tree' over ground produce — obviously invalid, so why teach it?
💡 Needed for Rabbi Yehuda, who says the tree Adam ate from was wheat (a child cannot say 'father' and 'mother' until tasting grain). One might think wheat gets 'fruit of the tree'

columns.label: Tree
columns.content: Take the fruit and the branch remains and produces again → 'fruit of the tree'

columns.label: Not a tree
columns.content: Take the fruit and no branch remains to produce again → 'fruit of the ground'

nodes.content: 🍷 'By whose word all things came to be' over everything: Rav Huna — except bread and wine; Rabbi Yoḥanan — even bread and wine

callout.label: Adam's tree, three views:
callout.text: Rabbi Meir: a vine, for nothing brings wailing like wine (Noah, Genesis 9:21). Rabbi Neḥemya: a fig, since they were repaired with fig leaves (Genesis 3:7). Rabbi Yehuda: wheat.

slides.title: 🍷 Does Shehakol Cover Bread and Wine?
slides.subtitle: The Gemara tries to map Rav Huna and Rabbi Yoḥanan onto Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei

lines.speaker: Tosefta
lines.text: Rabbi Meir: one who saw bread and said 'How pleasant is this bread, blessed is the Omnipresent Who created it' has fulfilled his obligation. Rabbi Yosei: whoever deviates from the formula the Sages coined has not fulfilled it.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: So Rav Huna (shehakol fails for bread and wine) is Rabbi Yosei, and Rabbi Yoḥanan (shehakol works even for them) is Rabbi Meir?

lines.speaker: Rav Huna
lines.text: I can hold even like Rabbi Meir. He validated a blessing that mentions bread by name; where the word bread is absent, even Rabbi Meir agrees one has not fulfilled his obligation.

lines.speaker: R' Yoḥanan
lines.text: And I can hold even like Rabbi Yosei. He rejected a blessing the Sages never instituted; shehakol is a blessing the Sages did institute, so even Rabbi Yosei agrees it works after the fact.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: Related: Rabbi Yehuda's 'Who creates various kinds of herbs' is not the halakha. His reason was 'Blessed is the Lord day by day' (Psalms 68:20) — give each day, and each food, its fitting blessing.

callout.label: Aggadic aside:
callout.text: Rabbi Zeira (or Rabbi Ḥinnana bar Pappa): a human vessel holds only when empty, but the Holy One fills the one who is already full — 'if you will surely listen, you will listen' (Exodus 15:26): listen to the old, and you will hear the new.

slides.title: 🐑 Binyamin the Shepherd's Aramaic Blessing
slides.subtitle: What must a blessing contain to count?

steps.content: 1️⃣ Binyamin the shepherd ate bread and said in Aramaic: בְּרִיךְ מָרֵיהּ דְּהַאי פִּיתָּא — 'Blessed is the Master of this bread'. Rav: he fulfilled his obligation
2️⃣ But Rav himself says a blessing without God's name is no blessing! Answer: he actually said 'Blessed is the All-Merciful, Master of this bread'
3️⃣ But Grace after Meals needs three blessings! Answer: he fulfilled only the first blessing

4️⃣ What is new? The mishna in Sota already lists Grace among things said in any language. Answer: one might think only a translation of the Sages' formula works — Rav teaches that even a different formula works after the fact
5️⃣ The core dispute: Rav — a blessing without God's name is no blessing; Rabbi Yoḥanan — a blessing without God's sovereignty is no blessing

6️⃣ Abaye sides with Rav: the tithe confession, 'I did not forget' (Deut. 26:13), means 'to mention Your name over it' — sovereignty is not taught. Rabbi Yoḥanan emends: 'Your name and Your sovereignty'

callout.label: Second mishna:
callout.text: Foods that do not grow from the ground (meat, fish, milk, eggs, cheese), spoiled foods, salt, brine, truffles and mushrooms all get shehakol. Mushrooms do grow from the ground, says Abaye, but they do not draw sustenance from it, so the baraita is read: 'that which does not draw sustenance from the ground'.

summary.principle: A blessing must serve the meal, name God, and fit the food — yet after the fact, a general blessing that the Sages instituted still counts, even in another language.

flowSteps.content: 🧂 Talk after hamotzi: 'take and bless' is fine for all; 'bring salt' is an interruption only for Rav; 'mix for the oxen' is fine only for Rav Sheshet, since animals are fed first
💊 Salt after eating, water after drinking; lentils and mustard monthly, small fish, black cumin by taste not smell
🌳 Mishna: 'fruit of the ground' covers tree fruit (land is primary — Rabbi Yehuda); 'fruit of the tree' never covers ground produce; shehakol covers all

columns.content: 🍷 Rav Huna: shehakol not for bread and wine. Rabbi Yoḥanan: even for them
🐑 Rav: a blessing needs God's name. Rabbi Yoḥanan: also His sovereignty

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Binyamin the shepherd fulfilled the first blessing of Grace in Aramaic with his own words — language and formula are not impediments after the fact

quiz.q: Why does Rav Sheshet hold that saying 'Mix the food for the oxen' after hamotzi is not an interruption?
o: Because animals are considered part of the household
Because it is forbidden to eat before feeding one's animals, so it serves the meal
Because any short statement is not an interruption
Because oxen are fed only with bread
quiz.e: Rav Sheshet relies on Rav Yehuda's ruling in Rav's name that one may not eat before feeding his animals, derived from the order of Deuteronomy 11:15; feeding them is thus part of preparing the meal.

quiz.q: How does the Gemara reconcile Rabbi Ḥama's praise of black cumin with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel calling it one of sixty deadly drugs?
o: One refers to fresh cumin and the other to dried
One refers to its taste and the other to its odor
One is the view of Eretz Yisrael and the other of Babylonia
One refers to eating it daily and the other once a month
quiz.e: Its taste is beneficial for the heart, while its odor is harmful; Rabbi Yirmeya's mother baked it into his bread and then peeled it off.

quiz.q: Which tanna holds that 'Who creates fruit of the ground' recited over fruit of a tree is valid after the fact, and why?
o: Rabbi Meir, because all fruits are equally fruit
Rabbi Yosei, because any instituted blessing works
Rabbi Yehuda, because the land is the primary factor in a tree's growth
Rabbi Neḥemya, because the tree of Adam was a fig
quiz.e: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak identifies the mishna with Rabbi Yehuda, who rules that even if the tree was cut down one still reads the first-fruits declaration, since the land is primary.

quiz.q: According to Rav Huna, over which foods does 'By whose word all things came to be' fail to fulfill one's obligation?
o: Fruit of the tree
Bread and wine
Vegetables
Meat and fish
quiz.e: Rav Huna excludes bread and wine from the mishna's 'over all of them'; Rabbi Yoḥanan holds shehakol works even for bread and wine.

quiz.q: What did Abaye cite to support Rav's view that a blessing requires mention of God's name but not His sovereignty?
o: The blessing of Binyamin the shepherd
The mishna in Sota listing texts said in any language
The tithe confession, 'I did not forget' — to mention Your name over it
The verse 'Blessed is the Lord day by day'
quiz.e: The baraita on Deuteronomy 26:13 explains 'I did not forget' as not forgetting to mention God's name, and says nothing of sovereignty; Rabbi Yoḥanan responds by emending the baraita.
